trust_decision.summary: Whether a terminal command may run is decided per request in the 'terminal' POST action: the whole command string is screened against a metacharacter blocklist, then prefix-matched against the TERMINAL_COMMANDS allowlist, before being interpolated into one shell string.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the terminal command allowlist; the only process sink in the repository (shell_exec) sits 42 lines below in the same case block, so a reader of the summary starts here.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST action=terminal (session + CSRF token at pheditor.php:303-311, permission 'terminal' at pheditor.php:576)
fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP action handler in a single-file PHP front controller

fix_sites.entry_point: called from the terminal handler; new helper terminal_tokenize($command)
called from the terminal handler; new helper terminal_extra_checks($binary, $tokens)
terminal widget keydown handler at pheditor.php:1691 -> POST response renderer at pheditor.php:1734-1747
fix_sites.module_kind: client-side JS renderer (response contract change for exit_code)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The allowlist is the feature: php, git, tar and composer are entries of TERMINAL_COMMANDS, so a solver can treat an allowed interpreter running its own options (php -r, git -c/--exec-path, composer run-script) as documented use rather than a bypass, and close only the report's example binary (find -exec).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Ordinary use of the allowlisted binaries with their normal options (php -d memory_limit=..., git -C <dir> status, git -c key=value, composer --working-dir) and the terminal's directory contract, where the server returns the post-command pwd as 'dir' and the widget sends it back on the next command; a fix that bans all dash-arguments, drops php/git/tar/composer from the allowlist, or stops returning dir removes the feature's purpose.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: pheditor.php:25; pheditor.php:617; pheditor.php:620-634; pheditor.php:1729-1733; pheditor.php:1738-1740; README.md:70

O6_input_shapes: bare command vs command with space-separated arguments (pwd vs ls -la): the binary must be the exact first argv token, not a string prefix (fix.diff:44-54)
double-quoted and single-quoted arguments containing spaces (find . -name "a b"), which the fix keeps as one argv element (fix.diff:149-160)
dangerous flag as a bare token vs flag=value vs subcommand form (-exec, --exec-path=/x, composer run-script) (fix.diff:64-70, fix.diff:72-81)
case variants of a blocked flag (-EXEC, -R, -F), matched case-insensitively with stripos (fix.diff:75, fix.diff:169)
git transport prefixes ext:: and fd:: inside a URL argument (fix.diff:167-173)
chmod setuid/setgid as symbolic (u+s) vs four-digit numeric (4755) (fix.diff:175-184)
shell redirection operators < and >, which the pinned metacharacter blocklist omits entirely, alongside the argument-injection shape (pheditor.php:588 vs fix.diff:145)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-binary argument policy for allowlisted binaries the published map omits (zip -T/--unzip-command, unzip, pkill -f)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: TERMINAL_COMMANDS is a documented admin-editable allowlist (README.md:70) and zip is already on it; adding one more binary to the feature is cheap, and the only place its argument policy can live is the same terminal handler.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a 'lint/run this file' action (php -l or php <file>) that reuses the terminal binary allowlist
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: pheditor is a PHP file editor with php already allowlisted, so a preview/execute button is an obvious next feature and would reuse the same allowlist and shell/proc_open path in the same switch.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a client-side command dispatcher that special-cases words (clear, exit) before the server check ever sees them
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the widget already intercepts two words locally and keeps history in a cookie, so local aliases or expansion would drift from the server's exact-argv check.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: server-echoed state (data.dir, pheditor.php:1738-1740) round-tripped back as the next request's dir with no server-side re-derivation
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix adds is_dir() at the sink (fix.diff:91) because the working directory is client-held state across requests; a 'recent commands' replay action would trust that same stored state.

O9_family: OS command injection / argument injection (CWE-78 + CWE-88): allowlist matched by string prefix and arguments trusted inside a shell string

O10_build.toolchain: PHP >= 8.3 (composer.json:21-23); one file pheditor.php, no composer install required; serve with php -S or php-fpm
O10_build.project_tests: none; the repository has no test suite and no CI test job (8 tracked files), and the fix diff adds no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep shell_exec and extend the blacklist (add -exec/-delete/-r/--exec-path for the binaries in the report) or run escapeshellarg over each token; the string is still built with the shell, so the metacharacter list that misses < and > and the prefix allowlist stay exploitable.

out_of_scope_notes: By design the editor can write .php files into the docroot (pheditor.php:340-372, pheditor.php:544-573), which is code execution without any shell; README.md:53 warns about it, and the terminal protection does not cover it.

The traversal guard at pheditor.php:321-329 url-decodes into the loop variable and never writes back to $_POST, and it only looks for '../', so the file actions still see the raw values; different sink, not pursued.
